claims.text: Listeriosis is caused by the bacterium Listeria monocytogenes.
claims.byte_quote: It is caused by the bacteria  Listeria monocytogenes .

claims.text: Listeriosis is rare, with 0.1 to 10 cases per 1 million people per year depending on country/region.
claims.byte_quote: It is a relatively rare disease with 0.1 to 10 cases per 1 million people per year depending on the countries and regions of the world.

claims.text: Highest-risk hosts for severe listeriosis are pregnant women, the elderly, and the immunocompromised (HIV, leukaemia, cancer, kidney transplant, steroid therapy).
claims.byte_quote: Pregnant women, the elderly or individuals with a weakened immune system, such as people with immuno-compromised status due to HIV, leukaemia, cancer, kidney transplant and steroid therapy, are at greatest risk of severe listeriosis and should avoid high risk foods.

claims.text: Invasive listeriosis affects high-risk groups: pregnant women, cancer/HIV/organ-transplant patients, the elderly, and infants.
claims.byte_quote: These include pregnant women, patients undergoing treatment for cancer, HIV and organ transplants, elderly people and infants.

claims.text: Invasive listeriosis symptoms include fever, myalgia, septicaemia, and meningitis; mortality is 20-30%.
claims.byte_quote: This form of disease is characterized by severe symptoms and a high mortality rate (20–30%). The symptoms include fever, myalgia (muscle pain), septicemia, meningitis.

claims.text: Pregnant women are about 20 times more likely to contract listeriosis than other healthy adults.
claims.byte_quote: Pregnant women are about 20 times more likely to contract listeriosis than other healthy adults.

claims.text: People with HIV are at least 300 times more likely to get listeriosis than the immunocompetent.
claims.byte_quote: People with HIV are at least 300 times more likely to get ill than those with a normally functioning immune system.

claims.text: Newborns may develop low birth weight, septicaemia, and meningitis from listeriosis.
claims.byte_quote: Newborn may also have low birth weight, septicaemia and meningitis.

claims.text: Diagnosis is by detecting the bacteria in a smear from blood, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), or meconium of newborns, among other specimens.
claims.byte_quote: detection of the bacteria in a smear from blood, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), meconium of newborns (or the fetus in abortion cases), as well as from faeces, vomitus, foods or animal feed

claims.text: Listeriosis is acquired mainly by eating contaminated food; can also transmit from pregnant woman to unborn baby.
claims.byte_quote: Eating contaminated food with high numbers of  L. monocytogenes  is the main route of infection. Infection can also be transmitted between humans, notably from pregnant women to unborn babies.

claims.text: High-risk food exposures include deli/ready-to-eat meats, soft cheeses, and cold-smoked fishery products.
claims.byte_quote: High risk foods include deli meat and ready-to-eat meat products (such as cooked, cured and/or fermented meats and sausages), soft cheeses and cold smoked fishery products.
